newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch PTT plans split proposal at AGM.
newsitem.headline: Dutch PTT plans split proposal at AGM.

text.p: Dutch post and telecoms group PTT Nederland NV said on Tuesday it planned to put a proposal for separate telecoms and post listings before its shareholders at its 1997 annual shareholders meeting early in 1998.

"We need the consent of the state in its role as holder of the special share. We don't need the special consent of the state as holder of a 45 percent stake because we need the consent of our annual shareholders' meeting anyway," KPN chairman Wim Dik said in an interview with Reuters.
Earlier on Tuesday Dutch PTT (KPN) said it planned to separate out the units by mid-1998.

"We will have a shareholders' meeting at the beginning of 1998 to approve our 1997 annual figures. Based on that there will be a proposal submitted to break up the company on the basis of a certain balance division and cost division. We will show two separate companies with their own accounts," said Dik.
"There will be a second shareholders' meeting to approve the breakup, sometime in the first half of next year," he added.
Dik said he would remain at the helm of KPN until the break up, while acting as head of PTT Telecom after the previously announced departure of Ben Verwaayen on September 1.
KPN said late last year it would review its structure with a view to a split. It has said it felt no need to hurry a decision which it had given itself until the end of 1997 to make.

Asked whether KPN had brought the decision forward Dik replied: "We think we went through the review quickly and carefully. We know that those two companies diverge more and more. Knowing that, and having the reputation as a management board which is proactive we'd rather do it now, although we could have waited another another year or two." -- Keiron Henderson, Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000
